atlas-my.0063: The TalentBank Career Fair was held on 1 August 2026 in Penang (internships, graduate programmes and full-time roles in business, accounting, engineering, IT and semiconductors), and the myStarjob Fair on 25 and 26 July 2026 in Johor Bahru; TalentCorp’s Minggu MyBakat is a talent-development week for students and fresh graduates.
atlas-my.0064: Windows differ by employer and are often open for long periods: CIMB’s Protégé takes applications all year round, its Complete Banker has intakes in April and October, and Khazanah moves candidates through online assessment, video, phone and final interviews as applications arrive.
atlas-my.0065: The programme pages read ask for a degree and a grade, not a master’s: Khazanah takes fresh graduates or final-year students of undergraduate or postgraduate study with a CGPA of at least 3.0, and CIMB’s Protégé asks for at least a diploma. Degree holders had a median monthly salary of RM5,724 against RM3,390 for diploma holders in 2024.
atlas-my.0066: The Malaysian Qualifications Register lists accredited programmes of local and foreign providers, and any interested party can use it to check the status of a qualification.
atlas-my.0067: The programme pages read name no target schools: CIMB, Khazanah and the Big Four set a minimum CGPA (3.25, 3.0 and about 3.0) and CIMB’s Complete Banker accepts all fields of study.
atlas-my.0068: The route into work is a short industrial training placement of usually 3 to 6 months, with allowances set by the organisation or under MySIP and the HRD Corp Industrial Training Scheme (up to RM500 a month); the pages read show no dual-study degree.
atlas-my.0069: The public service recruits through SPA with citizenship required, and government-linked groups such as Khazanah run their own graduate programmes; no headcount of graduate hires in the public sector was found in the pages read.
atlas-my.0070: Citizens-only schemes (Maybank, Khazanah, the public service) shut out foreigners, and the lowest Employment Pass category needs a basic salary of at least RM5,000 a month from 1 June 2026, above the RM4,521 median monthly salary of all graduates in 2024. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-my.0071: A photo is optional, but many local employers still expect a recent headshot on a plain background in business attire; multinationals can omit it. Leave off your full IC (MyKad) number, religion, race and exact date of birth.
atlas-my.0072: One to two pages; fresh graduates and people with under about 5 years of experience should aim for one page, and longer documents are discouraged outside academia and senior roles.
atlas-my.0073: The government guide on industrial training tells students to prepare an updated resume and a specific application letter; the programme pages read (CIMB, Khazanah) describe an online application with a CV and assessments.
atlas-my.0074: The pages read ask for a CV and assessments first; none of the programme stages read (Khazanah: CV, online assessment, video interview, phone interview, final interview) asks for referees up front.
atlas-my.0075: Applications ask for a CV and a result measure (CGPA, class or WAM) rather than certified copies; the public service sets qualification levels in its application requirements.
atlas-my.0076: Include your expected monthly salary in ringgit if the advert asks for it; if it does not, it can be left out and discussed at interview. The Malaysian Employers Federation warned in 2023 that graduate pay demands that are too high may not be affordable, putting honours-degree starting pay at about RM2,700 a month.
atlas-my.0077: No source read describes background checks for graduate programmes, so how routine they are is not established; qualification status can be checked in the Malaysian Qualifications Register.
atlas-my.0078: Formal schemes and public portals sit beside walk-in channels: SPA takes applications online, Khazanah runs a staged online process, and fairs such as myStarjob offer on-the-spot interviews and face-to-face networking.
atlas-my.0079: A foreign graduate faces citizens-only schemes and an Employment Pass whose lowest category needs RM5,000 a month from 1 June 2026, a pay level that entry roles rarely reach (the median graduate salary was RM4,521 in 2024).
atlas-my.0080: English is the default for private-sector and multinational roles; Bahasa Malaysia is sometimes required for government, government-linked and some local or front-line roles.
atlas-my.0081: Khazanah’s selection has five stages: application with CV, an online assessment, a recorded video interview, a phone interview and a final interview, and it may take a few months after applications close.
atlas-my.0082: CIMB’s Complete Banker also has five stages: online application, aptitude test, case study and group assessment, an interview with the Regional Head of Talent Acquisition and a final interview with the Group Chief People Officer.
atlas-my.0083: If the contract names no notice period, the Employment Act sets 4 weeks for under 2 years of service, 6 weeks for 2 years up to 5, and 8 weeks for 5 years or more; either party can end the contract by paying wages in lieu of notice.
atlas-my.0084: Public service appointments carry a probation period of 1 to 3 years; CIMB’s Protégé is a contract post of 8 months of on-the-job training after one week of classroom training.
atlas-my.0085: Pay expectations are modest: the median monthly salary of all graduates was RM4,521 in 2024 (RM5,724 for degree holders), while the Malaysian Employers Federation put honours-degree starting pay at about RM2,700 in 2023.
atlas-my.0086: Most graduate schemes read exclude foreigners: Maybank’s schemes are restricted to citizens, Khazanah is open to Malaysian citizens and the public service requires citizenship.
atlas-my.0087: Where an employer does sponsor, the Employment Pass has three categories from 1 June 2026: RM20,000 and above for up to 10 years, RM10,000 to 19,999 for up to 10 years with a succession plan, and RM5,000 to 9,999 for up to 5 years with a succession plan.
atlas-my.0088: No source read lists which employers sponsor graduates. Multinationals with large Malaysian sites, such as Intel in Penang (its largest site outside the United States, with about 9,000 Malaysians), are the places to ask; ask early and expect the question of pay level.
atlas-my.0089: Portals and boards: the SPA9 system for public service posts, SEEK Grad Malaysia (GradConnection), which showed 24 graduate and internship programmes the day it was read, and the career pages of CIMB, Khazanah and Maybank.
atlas-my.0090: Fairs: the TalentBank Career Fair (1 August 2026, Penang) and myStarjob (25 and 26 July 2026, Johor Bahru); university career offices and TalentCorp’s MySIP place students in industrial training.
atlas-my.0091: Skipping industrial training: it is the standard exposure to work before the degree, usually 3 to 6 months, and the national scheme sets a minimum allowance of RM600 a month.
atlas-my.0092: Applying to citizens-only schemes as a foreigner: Maybank’s schemes, Khazanah’s programme and public service posts require Malaysian citizenship.
atlas-my.0093: Putting your full IC (MyKad) number, religion or date of birth on the CV: the guide says never include the full IC number, because of identity-fraud risk.
atlas-my.0094: Expecting a high start: the median salary of all graduates was RM4,521 in 2024 and about 36% of tertiary-educated workers were in jobs below their skills.
atlas-my.0095: CIMB’s regional Complete Banker and the Protégé listing are in English; the pages read name no language test.
atlas-my.0096: The Big Four recruit in English; Bahasa Malaysia is not a stated requirement on the guides read.
atlas-my.0097: Bahasa Malaysia is sometimes required for government and government-linked roles, and the SPA pages and its application requirements are in Malay.
atlas-my.0098: Grab’s Kuala Lumpur R&D centre and the multinational plants in Penang work in English; the sources read name no language test.
atlas-my.0099: In 2024 Malaysia had 5.98 million graduates, 5.14 million of them in the labour force; graduate unemployment was 3.2% (165,900 people), about 67.8% of employed graduates were in skilled occupations, and skill-related underemployment of graduates was 32.2%.
atlas-my.0100: Early job absorption is weaker for graduates in education, services, agriculture, social sciences, journalism, information, and arts and humanities, while engineering, software and advanced manufacturing face talent shortages.
atlas-my.0101: No return-offer rate from industrial training to a graduate post was found in the pages read.
atlas-my.0103: All applications go through Education Malaysia Global Services: the university applies, you travel with the approval letter, and within seven working days of arrival take a medical including a urine drug test.
atlas-my.0104: No work during term; in breaks of more than seven days, up to 20 hours a week in restaurants, petrol stations, minimarkets or hotels only, and never as a cashier.
atlas-my.0105: about RM 2,760 to RM 3,220, medical and insurance included
atlas-my.0106: The pass is renewed only with 80% attendance and a CGPA of at least 2.00.
atlas-my.0108: Students of Malaysian universities intern on their Student Pass. Students of foreign universities need a Professional Visit Pass requested by the host company: typically 3 to 6 months, 12 at most, with an allowance but no salary. An internship as a tourist is illegal, even unpaid.
atlas-my.0110: A 12-month pass to look for work after a degree from a Malaysian university, open only to citizens of 32 listed countries, among them Germany, France, the Netherlands and the Nordic countries. Italy is not on the list.
atlas-my.0111: British graduates of Malaysian universities can get a 12-month pass to travel, work part time and look for a job.
